messages:
alex: heads-up, during Argos-30B int4 bring-up on dedicated we saw drift after ~32k tokens. not sure if it's RoPE scaling or KV retention leak. attaching quick notes.

mira: ugh. is this the longprefill case or streaming continuation?

alex: streaming continuation. sequence is: short system + 32k user context + followup — model starts repeating/losing coherence after token ~32720.

ryan: can you paste the minimal repro?

alex: sure — simplified thread: 
```
# config
model: argos-30b-int4
context_limit: 65536
rope_scaling: none (default)
kv_cache_mode: streaming

# input: system + 32768 token static prompt + incremental tokens
```
observed: reply diverges to repeated phrase and then emits earlier prefix text.

sylvia: does it reproduce with fp16 or is it int4-only?

alex: fp16 runs clean. int4 quant shows the issue consistently (5/5). fp16 on the same commit no problem.

mira: that strongly smells like quant kernel mismatch or index skew. on int4 kernels we do rounded rotary indexing slightly differently.

ryan: hypothesis: RoPE exponent scaling applied inconsistently between prefilling and streaming kernels (scale factor or offset). small phase mismatch will accumulate over longer windows and show as token drift.

alex: i dumped kv keys and noticed a subtle offset: prefill writes end at index 32767, streaming reads at 32769 for certain heads. gist: off-by-two on the write pointer in the int4 path. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T14:02:03Z] prefill: head0 kv_write idx=32767 token=...
[2026-03-21T14:02:03Z] stream: head0 kv_read idx=32769 token=...
```

sylvia: interesting. that would cause reads to pull stale positions and the RoPE phase applied to the wrong timestep.

mira: two immediate triage steps: 1) run the unit `kv-consistency-check --seed=seed1234 --model=argos-30b-int4` across CPU/GPU kernels, 2) run the same longprefill with `rope_debug=on` to log per-head phase deltas.

ops-bot: triggered job kv-consistency-check/6301239876 (queued).

alex: i've kicked off kv-consistency-check on a small canary node (dedicated-1). also running a full reproduce on dedicated-stable with trace enabled. link: https://internal-ci/runs/6301239876/trace

ryan: if it's an index write/read mismatch, quick fix may be in the int4 packing path where we compute the write stride. check prefetch tiling math and the tail-case that handles even/odd token counts.

mira: also check rotary scaling params: some older int4 optimize path applied `scale = banded ? 1.0004 : 1.0` to compensate quant bias — that stray constant could amplify.

alex: noted. priority is reproducer + kv dump. if we confirm, plan a hotfix to align write/read pointers and add a regression test under longprefill (50k token synthetic).

sylvia: can i own the regression test? i'll add a simple harness under eng-ml/tests/longprefill/ that runs argos-30b-int4, fp16, and compares logits + head-wise phase diffs.

mira: assigned sylvia for test. alex/ryan will handle kernel triage. ops-bot please canary the int4 patch on one dedicated shard before rolling.

ops-bot: canary scheduled: int4-kv-fix-canary on dedicated-1 at 2026-03-22T09:00:00Z.

alex: thanks. one more note — we saw occasional 'ghost' cache entries that survived eviction when using `prefill_stride=16`. probably related. i've added that to the triage checklist.

ryan: good capture. keep logs small but include per-head index and phase. that'll prove whether RoPE mismatch or stale KV reads.

mira: great. ping this thread when you have the kv dump link. :thumbsup:
